mainTopic: Why שבועת העדות applies only to monetary claims: the sources of the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי, and which money cases each one excludes.
overview: This amud asks why the oath of testimony (שבועת העדות) makes a witness liable only when the case is about money. It opens with the end of a ברייתא. A קל וחומר from the deposit oath (פקדון) is knocked down, and the rule is then proven with a גזירה שוה from the word תחטא. Next, רבה בר עולא challenges רבי אליעזר's proof from the repeated word או by pointing to the oath of utterance (שבועת ביטוי). The גמרא goes back and forth over which oath testimony resembles more, and decides on deposit because it shares more features. רבי עקיבא learns the rule from the word מֵאֵלֶּה, and the גמרא explains that he excludes some money cases: land, or, according to רבי יוחנן, fines. רבי יוסי הגלילי learns it from 'he saw or he knew'. The גמרא defends his view against רבי אחא's rule on circumstantial evidence, using the story of רבי שמעון בן שטח, and concludes that he exempts witnesses about a fine. The amud ends as רב יהודה begins a question about a loan given in front of witnesses, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A קל וחומר from the deposit oath to the testimony oath
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes a קל וחומר: the deposit oath is broad in many ways and still applies only to money, so the narrower testimony oath should certainly apply only to money.
steps.simpleTranslation: [A deposit oath applies to women and men alike and to all kinds of people, and he is liable] for each and every oath, whether in court or out of court, and still it only speaks about a monetary claim. Testimony, where the Torah did not treat women like men, relatives like non-relatives, or disqualified witnesses like qualified ones, and where he is liable for only one offering and only in court: isn't it logical that it should speak only about a monetary claim?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing an argument that started on the previous page. It says that if the wide-reaching deposit oath is limited to money cases, then the narrower testimony oath must surely be limited to money cases too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deposit oath (פקדון) covers everyone, brings a separate offering for each oath, and applies even outside court, yet it is still limited to money. The testimony oath is narrower in every one of these ways: only fit witnesses, one offering, and only in court. So by קל וחומר it should be limited at least as much, meaning to money cases only.

keyTerms.meaning: A monetary claim, a case about money
A deposit; here, the oath someone falsely swears to deny holding another's deposit
Treating relatives the same as non-relatives
Treating disqualified people the same as qualified ones
Is it not logical? This is the classic wording of a קל וחומר conclusion

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a sentence. The first words, "each and every one, before a court and not before a court," are still describing the deposit oath, not the testimony oath. The testimony half only begins with the word עדות.

phrases.english: for each and every one [oath],
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the previous page about the deposit oath: there, a person brings an offering for every single oath.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין וְשֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: whether before a court or not before a court,
it speaks only of a monetary claim;
testimony, regarding which [the Torah] did not make
women like men,
relatives like non-relatives,
disqualified like qualified;

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין –
phrases.english: and he is liable for only one [offering], [and only] before a court,
is it not logical that it should speak
only of a monetary claim?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא מְדַבֵּר אֶלָּא בִּתְבִיעַת מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's search for a source (begun on the previous daf) showing that שבועת העדות requires a monetary claim.
steps.raayaObject: That שבועת העדות applies only to monetary claims.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from שבועת הפקדון, which is broader in scope yet still limited to monetary claims.

steps.title: Refuting the קל וחומר: testimony is stricter in other ways
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר by showing two ways the testimony oath is actually stricter than the deposit oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a deposit? With a deposit, the Torah did not treat one who was made to swear like one who swore himself, or an intentional sinner like an unintentional one. Will you say the same about testimony, where the Torah did treat one who was made to swear like one who swore himself, and intentional like unintentional?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר from step 1. It shows that testimony is not narrower than a deposit in every way, so we cannot assume it is limited the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if one case is weaker than the other on every point. Here, testimony is stricter in two ways. A person is liable even if others made him swear (מושבע כנשבע). The Torah also treats a deliberate false oath the same as an accidental one (מזיד כשוגג), which it does not do for a deposit. Since testimony is broader in these ways, perhaps it also applies to cases that are not about money, so the proof falls.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The standard opening of a פירכא that breaks a comparison
Treating one who was made to swear by others like one who swore on his own
Treating an intentional sinner like an unintentional one
Will you say? It asks whether the same rule can really be applied

phrases.english: What about a deposit?
for with it [the Torah] did not make
one made to swear like one who swears himself
and intentional like unintentional;
phrases.notes: With a deposit, the Torah does not treat a deliberate false oath the same as an accidental one. With testimony, it treats them the same.

phrases.english: will you say [the same] about testimony,
for with it [the Torah] did make
one made to swear like one who swears himself, and intentional like unintentional?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְפִקָּדוֹן שֶׁכֵּן לֹא עָשָׂה בּוֹ מוּשְׁבָּע כַּנִּשְׁבָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the קל וחומר of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר entirely as a source.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Testimony is not weaker on every point: it is stricter regarding מושבע כנשבע and מזיד כשוגג, so the comparison breaks.

steps.title: The verbal analogy from the word 'shall sin'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves the rule with a גזירה שוה: the word תחטא appears for both testimony and deposit, so testimony is limited to money just like deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches 'shall sin'–'shall sin' for a verbal analogy. It says here [by testimony] 'shall sin,' and it says there [by deposit] 'shall sin.' Just as there it speaks only of a monetary claim, so too here it speaks only of a monetary claim.
steps.whatsHappening: Since logic (the קל וחומר) failed, the ברייתא turns to a word link in the פסוקים. The shared word תחטא connects testimony to deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה does not depend on the two cases being similar in strictness, so the refutation from step 2 does not affect it. The Torah uses the same word in both places, and that tells us to copy the rule: just as the deposit oath is about money, so is the testimony oath.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; it brings a source from the פסוק
Shall sin, the word shared by both sections
A verbal analogy: the same word in two places links their laws
Just as there... so too here; the standard way a גזירה שוה transfers a rule

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's final source that שבועת העדות requires a monetary claim is the גזירה שוה of תחטא–תחטא from שבועת הפקדון, after the קל וחומר was refuted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the oath of testimony only obligates a קרבן when the witness's testimony would have affected a money case.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
'shall sin' and 'shall sin,' for a verbal analogy:
it says here 'shall sin,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1, about the testimony oath.

phrases.english: and it says there 'shall sin';
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:21, about the deposit oath.

phrases.english: just as there it speaks
only of a monetary claim,
so too here it speaks
only of a monetary claim.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר תֶּחֱטָא תֶּחֱטָא לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logical proof is refuted, supplies a textual proof that is not affected by the refutation.
steps.raayaObject: That שבועת העדות applies only to monetary claims.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The גזירה שוה of תחטא in ויקרא 5:1 and ויקרא 5:21.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שבועת העדות is limited to monetary claims, learned through the גזירה שוה from פקדון.

steps.title: רבה בר עולא: the oath of utterance breaks רבי אליעזר's proof
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא challenges רבי אליעזר's derivation from the repeated או. The oath of utterance also has או–או, an oath, and no priest, yet it is not about money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא challenges it: The 'or... or' of the oath of utterance will prove otherwise. They are 'or's, they come with an oath, and there is no priest with them, yet they do not speak of a monetary claim!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to analyze an earlier opinion in the ברייתא, that of רבי אליעזר. רבה בר עולא attacks his proof, which learned testimony from deposit through the repeated word או.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said testimony should be learned from deposit because both have או, an oath, and no priest. רבה בר עולא points out that the oath of utterance (שבועת ביטוי) has exactly the same features, yet it is not limited to money. So these features alone cannot prove that testimony is limited to money; one could just as well learn from ביטוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges it; a sharp objection by an אמורא
Oath of utterance, a personal oath to do or not do something
Will prove; it brings a counterexample
The repeated uses of the word או, 'or'

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla challenges it:
the 'or'... 'or' of the oath of utterance will prove otherwise:
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:4.

phrases.english: for they are 'or's, and there is an oath with them,
and there is no priest with them,
yet they speak of a case that is not a monetary claim!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה בַּר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the end of the ברייתא back to analyzing רבי אליעזר's earlier derivation in it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's derivation, from או–או, that שבועת העדות requires a monetary claim, based on פקדון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבועת ביטוי shares all the features רבי אליעזר used (או, an oath, no priest) yet is not limited to monetary claims, so those features cannot decide that testimony follows פקדון.

steps.title: Better to learn from the deposit oath because both use the word תחטא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר rightly learned from the deposit oath, because both it and the testimony oath share the word תחטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense that he should learn from the deposit oath, since we can learn תחטא from תחטא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבה בר עולא's challenge. It says the testimony oath should be compared to the deposit oath, not to the oath of utterance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר עולא pointed out that the oath of utterance fits the או–או pattern too, and it is not about money. The answer is that the deposit oath has an extra link to testimony: the same word תחטא appears in both places. That extra link makes deposit the better model.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
Deposit (the deposit oath, שבועת הפקדון)
Utterance (the oath of utterance, שבועת ביטוי)
To learn / derive

phrases.english: It stands to reason he should learn from the deposit oath,
since it is "shall sin" from "shall sin."
phrases.notes: This is the same word link from step 3: "תחטא" is written for both the testimony oath and the deposit oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִפִּקָּדוֹן הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר עולא's challenge from step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Choosing the closer model: deposit has a shared word that utterance lacks
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The או–או pattern could point to the oath of utterance just as well as to deposit
steps.terutzMaskana: Deposit wins because it also shares the word תחטא

steps.title: Utterance and testimony both bring a sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the oath of utterance should be the model, since both it and the testimony oath bring a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from the oath of utterance, since it is a sin-offering case learned from a sin-offering case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues the other side. The oath of utterance also has a strong link to the testimony oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A false testimony oath and a false oath of utterance both require a קרבן חטאת. A false deposit oath requires a קרבן אשם instead. So the type of קרבן links testimony to utterance, which balances out the word link to deposit.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Sin-offering
Guilt-offering (brought for a false deposit oath)

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn from the oath of utterance,
since it is a sin-offering from a sin-offering!
phrases.notes: Both of these oaths bring a חטאת. A false deposit oath brings an אשם.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה – מִבִּיטּוּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 5's choice of deposit as the model
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that deposit is the more fitting model
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Utterance shares the same type of קרבן (חטאת) with testimony, while deposit brings an אשם

steps.title: Deposit shares a whole list of features with testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that deposit is still better, because it shares many features with testimony: the word חטא, liability when done on purpose, a claim and a denial, and an oath about the past.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it makes sense to learn from the deposit oath, since they share: sin; on purpose; he claimed from him and he denied him; and the past.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by listing several features that the deposit oath and the testimony oath have in common. The list is written as short memory words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each memory word stands for one shared feature. חטא is the shared word תחטא. במזיד means both bring a קרבן even when the false oath was on purpose. תבעיה וכפריה means in both, someone makes a claim and the swearer denies it. עבריה means both oaths are about something that already happened.

keyTerms.meaning: On purpose / intentionally
He claimed from him
He denied him
His past (an oath about past events)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִפִּקָּדוֹן הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף –
phrases.english: Rather, it stands to reason he should learn from the deposit oath,
since they share: sin; on purpose;
he claimed from him and he denied him; and his past.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִפִּקָּדוֹן הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 by showing that deposit has many links to testimony, not just one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One link each (תחטא for deposit, חטאת for utterance) leaves a tie
steps.terutzMaskana: Deposit has a whole group of links to testimony

steps.title: Utterance shares its own list of features with testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters that utterance also shares a list with testimony: a חטאת, a sliding-scale קרבן, and no extra fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from the oath of utterance, since they share: sin-offering; that goes down; and the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the list from deposit with a list from utterance. This list is also written as memory words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת means both bring a sin-offering. שירדה means both bring a קרבן עולה ויורד, a קרבן that goes up or down depending on what the person can afford. לחומש means neither pays an extra fifth, while a false deposit oath does require paying a חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: That goes down (a קרבן עולה ויורד, which depends on what the person can afford)
An extra fifth added to a payment
Sliding-scale offering

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn from the oath of utterance,
since they share: sin-offering; that goes down; the fifth!
phrases.notes: Again these are memory words. "The fifth" means neither oath pays an extra fifth, unlike the deposit oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִבִּיטּוּי הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 7 by offering a competing list of shared features
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Utterance also has a group of shared features with testimony, so deposit has no clear advantage

steps.title: Deposit's features are more numerous
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that deposit's shared features outnumber utterance's, so the testimony oath is learned from deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the back-and-forth. Deposit has more in common with testimony, so we learn from deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deposit list has more items than the utterance list. When two models compete, we choose the one with more shared features. So רבי אליעזר's derivation holds, and the testimony oath applies only to money matters.

keyTerms.meaning: These
They are more numerous

steps.whatToRemember: The testimony oath is compared to the deposit oath, not the oath of utterance. Deposit shares more features with it, so the testimony oath, like deposit, applies only to money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms רבי אליעזר's derivation and answers רבה בר עולא's challenge. It also shows a common way the גמרא picks between two possible sources: it counts the shared features.

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "These" means the features shared with the deposit oath from step 7.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ נְפִישָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 and closes the debate
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Deposit's shared features outnumber utterance's, so the testimony oath is limited to money, just like deposit.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the limit from the words 'of these'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reads the word מֵאֵלֶּה in the פסוק about the testimony oath as limiting. Some cases make the witness liable and some do not. A money claim makes him liable, and any other claim does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the פסוק says 'And it shall be when he will be guilty of one of these.' The word 'of these' teaches that for some of these he is liable and for some he is exempt. How? If the plaintiff asked him to testify about money, he is liable. If it was about something else, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives a different source than רבי אליעזר for the rule that the testimony oath applies only to money claims. He uses the word מֵאֵלֶּה, 'of these.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מֵאֵלֶּה means 'some of these,' not 'all of these,' so רבי עקיבא learns that the oath does not cover every kind of claim. He then decides which side is which: money claims bring liability and other claims do not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of these,' read as 'some of these,' which limits the rule
He demanded of him, meaning the plaintiff asked the witness to testify
Money, a monetary claim
Another matter, a claim that is not about money

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"And it shall be when he will be guilty of one of these"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:5

phrases.english: there are some of these for which he is liable,
and there are some of these for which he is exempt.
How so?
If he demanded money from him, he is liable;
phrases.notes: The plaintiff asked the witness to testify for him in a money case.

phrases.english: if he demanded another matter, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי אליעזר's source (from the deposit oath) is settled, the גמרא presents רבי עקיבא's separate source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From מֵאֵלֶּה: the testimony oath brings liability for money claims and not for other claims.

steps.title: Why not flip it the other way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word מֵאֵלֶּה only tells us that some cases are liable and some are exempt. It does not say which is which, so maybe other claims are liable and money claims are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will reverse it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: his word shows there is a split, but nothing in it tells us that money is the liable side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מֵאֵלֶּה proves only that the oath does not apply to everything. The challenge is that רבי עקיבא picked money as the liable side without a reason, and the opposite reading fits the word just as well.

keyTerms.meaning: I will reverse it, a challenge that the opposite reading works equally well

phrases.english: I will reverse it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיפוֹךְ אֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks how רבי עקיבא applied his own source in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's decision that money claims are the liable side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מֵאֵלֶּה shows only that there is a split, not which side gets liability. So the reverse reading is equally possible.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא also relies on רבי אליעזר's 'or's
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא already knows from רבי אליעזר's source, the repeated word או tied to the deposit oath, that money is the case covered. מֵאֵלֶּה then teaches something extra: even among money cases, some are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא relies on the 'or's of רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא does not flip the rule, because he accepts רבי אליעזר's source showing that money claims are the main case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money claims are already established from the או words that רבי אליעזר used, so reversing is not possible. That means רבי עקיבא's word מֵאֵלֶּה is not needed to set up the money rule. It is free to teach that some money cases are still exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'or's, the repeated word אוֹ in the פסוקים
Relies on

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא rejects רבי אליעזר's source. He accepts it, and he uses מֵאֵלֶּה for an extra point about money cases.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אַ״אוֹאִין״ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְמִיךְ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva relies on the "or"s of Rabbi Eliezer.
phrases.notes: These are the repeated words או that רבי אליעזר used to link testimony to the deposit oath, which is about money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אַ״אוֹאִין״ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר סְמִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'reverse it' challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an additional source that רבי עקיבא also accepts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מֵאֵלֶּה alone decides which side is liable, so the split could be read either way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The או words already set money as the case covered. מֵאֵלֶּה limits it further, so some money cases are exempt.

steps.title: What is the difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: Both agree that the oath is about money, and רבי עקיבא excludes some money cases. The גמרא asks what the practical difference between them is, meaning which money cases רבי עקיבא exempts.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them, between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by asking where these two תנאים actually disagree in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 showed that רבי עקיבא accepts רבי אליעזר's source and adds an exclusion with מֵאֵלֶּה. So there must be some money case where רבי אליעזר says liable and רבי עקיבא says exempt, and the גמרא wants to identify it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּבֵין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא?
phrases.english: between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ בֵּין רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וּבֵין רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 12: since רבי עקיבא adds an exclusion, the גמרא asks what it changes in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which money cases רבי עקיבא exempts that רבי אליעזר would hold liable.

steps.title: The difference is witnesses about land
steps.stepSummary: The difference between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is when someone makes witnesses swear about land. רבי אליעזר makes them liable, and רבי עקיבא exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is someone who makes witnesses swear about testimony involving land. According to רבי אליעזר they are liable, and according to רבי עקיבא they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. It names the money case that רבי עקיבא excludes: testimony about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, every money case is covered by the testimony oath, including land. For רבי עקיבא, the word מֵאֵלֶּה cuts some money cases out, and land is one of them.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them
One who makes someone take an oath
Witnesses whose testimony is about land
They are liable (they must bring a קרבן if they swore falsely)
They are exempt

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
one who makes witnesses swear about land —
according to רבי אליעזר, they are liable;
according to רבי עקיבא, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ מַשְׁבִּיעַ עֵדֵי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 13 by naming the case where the two תנאים disagree.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses about land: liable according to רבי אליעזר, exempt according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: What is the difference according to רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds elsewhere that even רבי אליעזר exempts witnesses about land. So according to him, land cannot be the difference. What is the difference then?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יוחנן, who says there that one who makes witnesses swear about land, even according to רבי אליעזר they are exempt, what difference is there here between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the last answer does not work according to רבי יוחנן. It asks for a different case that would separate the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said in another discussion that land witnesses are exempt even for רבי אליעזר. If so, both רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא exempt land, and the answer in step 14 falls away. The גמרא needs a new money case where only רבי עקיבא exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: There (in a different discussion)
Here (in our discussion)
Even

phrases.english: And according to רבי יוחנן, who said there:
phrases.notes: "There" means a different discussion about the deposit oath and the testimony oath.

phrases.english: one who makes witnesses swear about land,
even according to רבי אליעזר they are exempt —
here, what difference is there
between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer of step 14 does not fit רבי יוחנן's view, and asks the question of step 13 again for his view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יוחנן, which money case does רבי עקיבא exempt that רבי אליעזר holds liable?

steps.title: The difference is witnesses about a fine
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוחנן, the difference is witnesses whose testimony is about a fine (קנס). רבי אליעזר makes them liable, and רבי עקיבא exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is witnesses about a fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 15 with a new case: testimony about a fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fine is a payment of money, so רבי אליעזר includes it in the testimony oath. רבי עקיבא uses מֵאֵלֶּה to exclude it, so for him witnesses about a fine are exempt. This gives a real difference between the two even for רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses whose testimony would make someone pay a fine
A fine, a set payment that the תורה imposes, not simply repaying a loss

steps.whatToRemember: The two תנאים agree that the testimony oath is about money. רבי עקיבא excludes certain money cases: land (step 14), or fines (step 16, according to רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: There is a difference between them: witnesses about a fine.
phrases.notes: Meaning: רבי אליעזר holds such witnesses liable, and רבי עקיבא exempts them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ עֵדֵי קְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 with a different case that fits רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses about a fine: liable according to רבי אליעזר, exempt according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: 'he saw or he knew' points to money testimony
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי brings a new source. The פסוק says 'he saw or he knew', so it must be talking about testimony that can stand on seeing alone or on knowing alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי says: 'And he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew.' The פסוק is speaking about testimony that can be established by seeing without knowing, or by knowing without seeing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new opinion begins. רבי יוסי הגלילי gives his own source, different from רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, for limiting the testimony oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'or' means either seeing alone or knowing alone is enough to make someone a witness. Money testimony can work that way, while other kinds of testimony need both seeing and knowing. So the פסוק is about money testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Seeing (the witness saw the event)
Knowing (the witness knows the facts without having seen them happen)
Testimony
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.english: רבי יוסי הגלילי says:
"And he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:1

phrases.english: about testimony that stands on seeing without knowing
and on knowing without seeing
the פסוק is speaking.
phrases.notes: He means money testimony, since other kinds of testimony need both seeing and knowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, separate source for the same idea, after the discussion of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the פסוק allows seeing alone or knowing alone, the testimony oath covers testimony that works that way, which is money testimony.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי הגלילי reject רבי אחא's camel ruling?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks whether רבי יוסי הגלילי disagrees with רבי אחא, who rules from circumstantial evidence. If he agreed, capital cases could also have 'knowing without seeing.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Should we say רבי יוסי הגלילי does not hold like רבי אחא? רבי אחא taught: if a wild camel is rampaging among camels and a dead camel is found next to it, we know this one killed it. If רבי יוסי הגלילי held like רבי אחא, then in capital cases too you could find 'knowing without seeing,' like the case of רבי שמעון בן שטח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's claim from Step 17 that only money cases allow testimony from knowing alone. He points to רבי אחא's rule, which would allow it in capital cases too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אחא says that circumstantial evidence, like a dead camel next to a rampaging one, counts as 'knowing' who did it. If that kind of knowing also works in capital cases, then capital cases have 'knowing without seeing,' and רבי יוסי הגלילי's reason for limiting the oath to money cases falls apart. So it seems רבי יוסי הגלילי must reject רבי אחא.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (it opens a suggestion that the גמרא will test)
He does not hold of (an opinion)
A wild, rutting male camel
It is clearly known
Capital cases (life-and-death cases)
You can find such a case

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Shall we say that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili
does not hold like Rabbi Acha?
As it is taught: Rabbi Acha says:
A rampaging camel among the camels
and a camel was found killed at its side,
it is known that this one killed it.
For if he holds like Rabbi Acha,
in capital cases too you can find it,
phrases.notes: 'It' means testimony from knowing without seeing.

phrases.english: like the case of Rabbi Shimon ben Shatach!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of רבי יוסי הגלילי from Step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's claim that only money cases allow testimony from knowing alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רבי אחא, circumstantial evidence creates 'knowing' even in capital cases, so capital cases would also fit 'or he knew.'

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן שטח's story: the man with the bloody sword
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן שטח swears he saw a man chase another into a ruin and then found him with a dripping sword next to the dying victim.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון בן שטח said: May I not see the comfort of Israel if I did not see a man run after his fellow into a ruin. I ran after him and found a sword in his hand, blood dripping, and the victim twitching. I said to him: Wicked one! Who killed this man? Either me or you!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the story that רב פפא mentioned, as an example of a capital case built on clear 'knowing' without actually seeing the killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן שטח did not see the stabbing itself, but the evidence left no doubt who the killer was. This is exactly 'knowing without seeing' in a murder case, which supports רב פפא's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath: 'May I (not) see the comfort of Israel if...'
A ruin, an abandoned building
Sword
Twitching, convulsing (as one dying)

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Shatach said:
May I see the consolation
phrases.notes: This is a way of swearing. It means 'May I NOT see the comfort of Israel if this isn't true.'

phrases.english: if I did not see one person
who ran after his fellow into a ruin,
and I ran after him,
and I found a sword in his hand
and blood dripping
and the slain man twitching;
I said to him: Wicked one!
Who killed this man?
Either me or you!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the case רב פפא pointed to
steps.raayaObject: That capital cases can involve 'knowing without seeing'
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן שטח

steps.title: No execution without two witnesses, but Heaven punishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן שטח says he cannot have the man executed, because the תורה requires two witnesses. Heaven will punish him, and a snake kills him on the spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what can I do? Your blood is not handed over to me, because the תורה said: 'By the word of two witnesses or three witnesses shall the one who is to die be put to death.' Rather, ה' will punish you. They said: they did not move from there until a snake bit him and he died.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי שמעון בן שטח explains why a human court cannot execute the killer, and Heaven punishes him instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן שטח himself did not execute the man, because the תורה requires actual eyewitnesses. In the גמרא's discussion, though, the story serves as the example of 'knowing without seeing' in a capital case. Under רבי אחא's approach, that kind of evidence could count.

keyTerms.meaning: Your blood is not handed over to me (I have no power to execute you)
ה' (literally 'the Place')
Will punish, will collect payment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't conclude that the court could execute based on the story. רבי שמעון בן שטח himself says he cannot. The גמרא only uses the story as an example of 'knowing without seeing' in a murder case.

phrases.english: But what can I do,
since your blood is not handed over to me,
for the Torah said:
"By the word of two witnesses
or three witnesses shall the one to die be put to death."
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6

phrases.english: Rather, God will punish you.
They said: they did not move from there
until a snake bit him and he died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה, שֶׁאֵין דָּמְךָ מָסוּר בְּיָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A human court cannot execute without two eyewitnesses. Heaven punished the killer.

steps.title: Capital cases never have 'seeing without knowing'
steps.stepSummary: Even if רבי יוסי הגלילי accepts רבי אחא, capital cases still fail. Seeing alone is never enough there, because witnesses must know who the victim was and his condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say he holds like רבי אחא: granted, you can find knowing without seeing in capital cases. But how can you find seeing without knowing? Don't the witnesses need to know whether he killed a gentile or a Jew, and whether he killed a טריפה person or a healthy one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא. רבי יוסי הגלילי can agree with רבי אחא, because capital cases still lack the other half of the פסוק: seeing without knowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'he saw or he knew' needs testimony that can work from either one alone. In a murder case, just seeing the act is never enough. The witnesses must also know facts that decide whether the death penalty applies, such as whether the victim was a Jew and whether he was whole and not a טריפה. Only money cases fit both halves, so רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say
Granted, it works out well for
Knowing without seeing
Seeing without knowing
A person with a fatal injury, expected to die within twelve months

steps.whatToRemember: Under רבי יוסי הגלילי, the oath of testimony needs cases where seeing alone OR knowing alone can be enough. Capital cases can have knowing without seeing, but never seeing without knowing. So only money cases qualify.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves רבי יוסי הגלילי's source from Step 17 without forcing him to reject רבי אחא's rule about circumstantial evidence.

phrases.english: Even if you say
that he holds like Rabbi Acha;
granted, knowing without seeing,
you can find it;
phrases.notes: He means: even in capital cases, as in רבי שמעון בן שטח's story.

phrases.english: but seeing without knowing,
how can you find it?
Don't they need to know

phrases.aramaic: אִם גּוֹי הָרַג אוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל הָרַג,
phrases.english: whether he killed a gentile or he killed a Jew,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָדָם טְרֵפָה הָרַג אוֹ שָׁלֵם הָרַג?
phrases.english: whether he killed a fatally injured person or he killed a whole one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge from Step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the premise but points to a missing second requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting רבי אחא would make capital cases fit 'or he knew,' which would break רבי יוסי הגלילי's limit to money cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק needs both seeing-alone and knowing-alone. Capital cases can never be based on seeing alone, so they are still excluded.

steps.title: Witnesses to a fine are exempt in the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that witnesses about a קנס who falsely swear they know nothing are פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that if someone makes witnesses about a fine swear, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes what it just learned about capital cases and applies it to cases of a קנס (a fine). Its conclusion is that רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts these witnesses from שבועת העדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 showed that capital cases fall outside the פסוק because seeing alone is never enough there. The גמרא now says the same is true for fines. So under רבי יוסי הגלילי, a false oath by witnesses about a קנס carries no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this; a conclusion drawn from what came before
One who makes someone take an oath
Witnesses whose testimony would make someone pay a fine set by the Torah
Exempt; here, not liable for a קרבן for a false oath

phrases.english: Conclude from it
that Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds:
one who makes witnesses about a fine swear — they are exempt;

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, קָסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the reasoning used to exclude capital cases (step 21) to cases of a קנס.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, witnesses about a קנס who swear falsely are not liable for שבועת העדות.

steps.title: Why fines fail the 'seeing alone' test
steps.stepSummary: Even if knowing without seeing works for fines, seeing without knowing does not. The witnesses must know whether the woman was Jewish and whether she was a virgin.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you think the witnesses are liable: granted, we can find knowing without seeing. But seeing without knowing? Don't they need to know whether he was with a non-Jewish woman or a Jewish woman, with a virgin or a non-virgin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the conclusion of step 22. A fine case fails one of the two tests the פסוק requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ראה או ידע' covers only testimony that can stand on ראיה alone and on ידיעה alone. In a קנס case, ידיעה without ראיה can work, like the circumstantial evidence of רבי אחא. But ראיה alone is never enough, because the fine applies only to a Jewish girl who was a virgin, so the witnesses must also know who she was.

keyTerms.meaning: For if you would think; introduces the opposite idea in order to reject it
Granted; admits one point before showing a problem
Seeing without knowing; witnessing the act without knowing the background facts
A virgin
A woman who is not a virgin

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying fines can never be proven. Fines can be proven. The point is only that seeing alone can never prove them, so they don't fit the פסוק's 'he saw OR he knew'.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי הגלילי, שבועת העדות applies only where testimony can stand on seeing alone and on knowing alone. Capital cases and fines both fail the 'seeing alone' test, so they are excluded.

phrases.english: For if it would enter your mind that they are liable,

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי דִּידִיעָה בְּלֹא רְאִיָּה – אַשְׁכְּחַן לַהּ;
phrases.english: granted that knowing without seeing — we find it;
phrases.notes: Like the case of רבי אחא from step 18, where we rely on circumstantial evidence without anyone seeing the act.

phrases.english: but seeing without knowing —
don't they need to know
whether he had relations with a non-Jewish woman or with a Jewish woman,
whether he had relations with a virgin or with a non-virgin?
phrases.notes: The fine is paid only for a Jewish girl who was a virgin, so seeing the act alone can't settle it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the conclusion stated in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יוסי הגלילי exempts עדי קנס
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic from the פסוק 'ראה או ידע' (step 17): fine cases cannot be proven by seeing alone, since the woman's identity and status must be known.

steps.title: רב יהודה begins a question about a loan given in front of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא is sitting before רב יהודה, who raises a question about a man who says, 'I counted out a מנה to you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא was sitting before רב יהודה, and רב יהודה sat and was asking: 'I counted out a מנה to you in front of so-and-so and so-and-so...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion. This line sets the scene and starts רב יהודה's question; the rest of the question comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here we talked about fines and capital cases. Now the גמרא turns to an ordinary money case, a loan. The claimant names specific witnesses, which prepares the question of what those witnesses would have to see or know.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him; in front of him, as a student before a teacher
He was asking a question he was unsure about
A sum of money, one hundred זוז
So-and-so and so-and-so; stands in for named people, here the witnesses

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna was sitting before Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב יְהוּדָה וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ:
phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda was sitting and raising a question:
"I counted out a maneh to you
in front of so-and-so and so-and-so",

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב הַמְנוּנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from fines and capital cases to a new question about an ordinary money case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setup only: a claimant says he gave a מנה in front of named witnesses. The actual question continues in the next lines.
